fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeNiMn-Al composition and SPD/annealing route do not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiTi powder-metallurgy route based on high-energy ball milling and spark-plasma sintering.
No cited evidence demonstrates that only 0.5-1.0 at.% Al in CoCrFeMnNi can produce 5-15 vol% disordered BCC while retaining an FCC matrix; this central phase-constitution claim is unsupported.

Evidence E1 concerns B2/BCC decomposition in AlCoFeNi-derived alloys rather than FCC/BCC formation in dilute-Al CoCrFeMnNi, and it includes an ordered B2 phase contrary to the stated objective of avoiding ordered intermetallics.

The baseline characterization of cast CoCrFeMnNi as intrinsically limited in ductility conflicts with E2, which describes the equiatomic Cantor alloy as having excellent elongation and fracture toughness.

The proposed falsification experiment cannot cleanly distinguish phase-boundary strengthening from grain-size, recovery, segregation, and dislocation-density effects because SPD-only and annealed samples will differ in all of these variables.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested generic targets—sub-50 nm grains, a nominal FCC/BCC structure, high yield strength, intermetallic suppression, boundaries, and a test—but it diverges completely from the hidden material and processing target. The target uses equimolar CoCrFeNiTi powders, high-energy ball milling at 400 rpm and 20:1 ball-to-powder ratio, followed by SPS at 900-1000°C, producing approximately 83% FCC/17% BCC and measured hardness and strength near 675 HV and 1894 MPa. The generated proposal instead substitutes a dilute-Al Cantor alloy and SPD plus 400-600°C annealing. Generic Hall-Petch and dislocation-strengthening concepts overlap with the target mechanism, but the claimed deformation-induced BCC transformation, dilute-Al phase stability, solute-drag stabilization, and stated instability thresholds are not established by the supplied evidence. E3 only supports broad effects of Al and Ti in other HEAs, while E1 concerns a compositionally different B2/BCC system. The experiment is useful for checking grain size and phase formation, but stronger discrimination would require matched samples with comparable grain size and dislocation density but different BCC fractions, followed by quantitative strength decomposition or in situ annealing measurements.
